`DESKTOP_RELEASE.md`:

```md
# NullCS desktop beta

## 0.1.0-beta.2 — score context and report charts

This update changes presentation only: direct project wording, interactive player score bars, and an anonymous histogram of the historical CS2CD player-model out-of-fold predictions. The original parser, features, models, calibration, scoring, and ranking are unchanged; the frozen backend is reused after all 61 manifest hashes and packaged Python sources were checked against this checkout.

`main/ui/web/scripts/export-score-reference.py --data-root <processed-root>` reproduces `src/lib/score-reference.json` from the saved OOF CSV and evaluation summary. It checks all four confusion matrices, finite scores, class totals, and one fold per demo. Only aggregate counts and provenance hashes ship; player identifiers and raw training rows do not. This is historical grouped player-model evaluation, not a new independent end-to-end test.

Green (<20), yellow (20 to <50), and red (>=50) are display bands for **raw model score / 100**, selected from existing evaluated cutoffs. They are not optimized decision thresholds, cheating categories, or changes to the inference pipeline. Calibration/review scores do not inherit these colors. A model-hash mismatch disables reference bands and population comparisons. The chart normalizes each label group separately, uses unsmoothed five-point bins, and exposes counts and threshold tradeoffs. At 50: TP 846, FP 301, FN 146, TN 5,593. Dataset labels, prevalence, and patch differences affect interpretation. Multi-demo player analysis remains planned, not implemented.

Validation: two focused report tests passed (boundaries, invalid scores, unmatched models, histogram totals); desktop frontend and native installer builds passed. Real-demo native validation rendered ten players and 20 distribution bins, exercised score-type/player selection and keyboard bin selection, with no page errors. Website production build and desktop/mobile copy/navigation checks passed. Interactive charts are inside the app; the saved report remains plain text. No new runtime dependencies were added; the desktop production npm audit reported zero findings. Existing development/build-tool advisories remain.

Beta.2 installer SHA-256: `4a76532f0f99ce9785348ff1f21bd6e067cc982302fbdb27f0fcd407e463a9ea`. It remains unsigned with manual updates; the signing and clean-machine limitations below still apply. Older beta.1 artifact records below are historical.

**Community beta distribution (October 10, 2026):** this GPLv3 GitHub prerelease is unsigned. The site and release notes disclose the unknown-publisher status and manual updates. This community-beta path supersedes the earlier blanket hold on unsigned downloads; the fully signed release procedure remains available for future releases. Automatic updates stay disabled until signing keys/feed are configured; no verification bypass is permitted. Clean-machine certification remains unverified. LICENSE, NOTICE.md and collected third-party notices accompany the distribution.

The release candidate is `NullCS_0.1.0-beta.1_x64-setup.exe`, **389,857,409 bytes**, SHA-256 `0f45bba38cd497f03e30c945b120a358ccfec6165c667c92d69950d94b3ac326`. It includes GPLv3 and third-party notices (593 dependency inventory records). All 61 backend manifest hashes passed; the final frozen engine processed the validation demo into ten ranked players in **37.27 seconds** on the developer workstation. Defender completed a targeted scan with no detection event observed during that scan. These checks do not establish clean-machine compatibility or eliminate all security risks.

Release location: https://github.com/gjones01/NullCS/releases/tag/v0.1.0-beta.1. The installer contains the runtime/models; the separate model ZIP is for developers rebuilding the corresponding source tag. Verify assets against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Earlier dated entries below are historical validation records: their installer hashes, unpublished status and blanket signing gates are superseded by this explicitly unsigned beta policy. The signed-update procedure and unresolved parser, calibration, maintenance, build-tool and clean-machine limitations still apply.

The active desktop entry point is `main/ui/web/src/DesktopApp.tsx`. It replaces the old multi-page UI at startup; the previous `App.tsx` and research explanation components remain in the repository but are not imported into the client bundle. `/analyze` on the Next.js site is now the Windows download page. No hosted inference server is required for this product path.

## Local workflow

Windows x64: choose or drop one CS2 `.dem` (maximum 1 GiB), run local analysis, read ranked players, and save a plain-text report through the native Save dialog. The score guide defines each displayed value. Explanations are not generated. Research warnings remain visible under report limitations and are included in the saved report. Scores are not cheating verdicts.

The Tauri shell starts an authenticated, loopback-only FastAPI sidecar with a random per-launch token held in memory. The UI uses native drag/drop and file selection. The engine checks the file header, size, and extension. The canonical boundary remains `main/scripts/run_infer_pipeline.py`, invoked through the packaged `run-infer` command. `/api/desktop/demo/{id}/result` reads the canonical per-demo CSV, manifest, and score trace without re-sorting, recomputing scores, generating explanations, or loading interpretation dataframes. Null calibration stays null. Features, model weights, calibration, sequence construction, and ranking formulas are unchanged.

States follow actual pipeline logs: queued, parsing, feature processing, temporal inference, scoring, results ready; failures remain explicit. A serial executor lock protects shared ranking writes. A native single-instance lock prevents two clients sharing the same data directory. Interrupted jobs fail on startup; the child watches its parent pipe and exits if the API dies. Normal application exit and update installation stop the API process tree. In packaged builds, the API also watches a pipe owned by the desktop shell and exits if that shell crashes. Polling is every 2.5 seconds, below the default request refill rate.

Local storage is `%APPDATA%/app.nullcs.desktop/backend-data/`: `raw_uploads`, `processed`, and `state`. Demos/reports persist locally. There is no automatic deletion policy yet; users can remove this directory after closing NullCS, which also removes their analysis history. No telemetry is added. Updates are the intended external network access; they do not upload demos. Input files are untrusted: run the app without administrator privileges. A local parser process is not a hardened OS sandbox.

## Visuals and performance

Black/blue glass panels, pointer-reactive orbital particles, and quiet opt-in synthesized interaction tones. Sound defaults off. Motion can be disabled and respects OS reduced-motion settings; the canvas is capped at approximately 30 redraws/second and DPR 1.5, pauses when hidden or analyzing, and does not rerender React per animation frame. The frontend excludes the former Three.js scene, marketing videos, bundled samples, and explanation UI. `publicDir: false` prevents unused public assets being copied into the desktop bundle.

No inference feature or numerical optimization was introduced. The existing CLI still loads its models and parses the demo using the established methodology. Packaging currently uses the existing PyInstaller one-file approach, which adds extraction/startup overhead. Keep that overhead in capacity/runtime measurements; do not call browser bundle size an inference speedup.

## Artifact integrity and updates

Local models cannot be kept secret from the machine owner. This design protects distribution integrity, not confidentiality or resistance to an administrator modifying the application.

- Release builds only resolve the verified packaged backend; they cannot fall back to `C:/NullCS` or another source checkout.
- The application embeds the backend manifest SHA-256. Native streaming SHA-256 verifies listed files before launching the sidecar. Changed cached model files are refreshed from the verified package at launch; canonical model files are required during packaging.
- Only the eight verified default model artifacts are copied into the release payload. Experimental model variants, secrets, demo datasets, and training caches are not part of that selection. Research CLI override behavior is unchanged; the distribution intentionally ships the canonical bundle.
- Do not edit generated resources after building the application. Re-run `scripts/prepare-desktop-backend.ps1` whenever Python, parser, model, or dependency content changes.
- The updater uses Tauri's signature verification, HTTPS, a build-pinned public key and endpoint, and signed-version enforcement. There is no unsigned fallback or URL supplied by browser content. Checks run at launch, every six hours while visible/idle, and on demand. Installation requires a click and is disabled while analysis is running. An offline check failure does not disable local analysis.
- Updates ship the whole tested app/backend/model bundle. No client-side `pip install` or independent parser/model replacement occurs. CS2 schema mismatches fail rather than filling missing model inputs.

The PyInstaller hooks explicitly collect SciPy array-API compatibility modules, XGBoost native libraries and its VERSION file, and parser/XGBoost/pandas distribution metadata. Each package must pass a `check-runtime` import and provenance smoke test before its manifest is generated.

Dependencies added: Rust `sha2` for native hashing (replacing per-file certutil subprocesses), and `tauri-plugin-updater` pinned to 2.12.0 for signed updates. Cargo.lock includes its required transitives. Rust minimum is 1.90; validation used 1.94.1. No Python or ML dependency versions were upgraded. Standard release builds must have the same tested Python 3.13 environment/artifacts used to rebuild the sidecar.

## Release setup (not yet provisioned)

Use the isolated desktop release runtime, not the research virtual environment. On Windows x64 with Python 3.13, create a fresh virtual environment and install `main/ui/web/scripts/requirements-desktop.lock.txt` with `pip install --only-binary=:all: -r ...`. Set `NULLCS_RELEASE_PYTHON` to its absolute `Scripts/python.exe` path. This build-only setting selects the same interpreter for audit, tests, and packaging. The runtime verifier rejects missing, changed, or extra packages. The current local validated environment is `C:\ClarityCS\main\data\web_validation\release-venv`; it is generated and must not be committed. Keep audit tooling in a separate environment selected by `NULLCS_AUDIT_PYTHON`.

GitHub release repository: https://github.com/gjones01/NullCS. No release has been published by this change. GitHub write access can be granted with the GitHub connector or `gh auth login`; never paste a token into chat or the repository.

1. Generate a Tauri signing key with the installed Tauri CLI signer, keep the private key/password in secure release secrets, and back it up. Set `NULLCS_UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY` to the public key contents. This is separate from Windows signing.
2. Configure a Windows code-signing certificate/service and timestamp service. The provided release script supports a certificate thumbprint in the Windows certificate store. Other signing services need their documented sign-command integration.
3. Set `NULLCS_UPDATE_ENDPOINT` to a public HTTPS `latest.json` release feed. For GitHub, a latest-release asset URL can serve it; use a deliberate channel for prereleases because GitHub's latest-release alias does not select prereleases. The URL must be reachable without embedding a repository access token in the client.
4. Supply `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`, optional `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`, `NULLCS_WINDOWS_CERT_THUMBPRINT`, and `NULLCS_WINDOWS_TIMESTAMP_URL` in the release shell/secret store. `NULLCS_UPDATE_ENDPOINT` and `NULLCS_UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY` are public build inputs embedded into Rust; all signing private credentials stay outside the application.
5. Install `cargo-audit` on the release runner's PATH, and install `pip-audit` in a separate tooling virtual environment (not the model environment). Set server/operator-only `NULLCS_AUDIT_PYTHON` to that environment's Python executable. Put Windows SDK `signtool.exe` on PATH. Dependency audits require access to their advisory services; failures block release. Bump the version in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` and `Cargo.toml`. From `main/ui/web`, run:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/build-signed-release.ps1 -InstallerUrl 'https://github.com/gjones01/NullCS/releases/download/<tag>/<actual-installer-name>.exe'
```

The script runs Python/Rust/frontend dependency audits and backend/native regression tests before building. It rebuilds the backend and frontend, generates Tauri update artifacts, and requires valid timestamped Windows signatures on the installer, native application, and backend executable. The backend is signed before its integrity manifest is generated. Stale installers are rejected. It writes `latest.json` but does not upload or publish anything. The update signature must contain a signed version matching the feed; use a Tauri CLI that supports version-bound signatures and verify the update from the previous installed release before publication. Missing configuration fails the release preparation explicitly.

6. Test a clean Windows machine without Python: install, startup, actual demo, report save, corrupt file, second instance, restart, and update from the previous version. Verify a tampered updater payload is rejected, TLS errors do not bypass validation, and model hashes match the published bundle. This is a release gate, not replaced by unit tests.
7. Publish the verified installer, its `.sig`, and `latest.json` as public release assets. Preserve old releases for rollback investigation; the updater does not enable downgrades.
8. After publishing and verifying the release asset, update `main/ui/site/src/lib/published-desktop-release.json` with its exact URL, version and checksum, then deploy the website. The optional server-side `NULLCS_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL` overrides that versioned public configuration; setting it to an empty string disables downloads. Both paths use the strict HTTPS `.exe` release-URL validator for `gjones01/NullCS`. Never record an unpublished asset as the default. Vercel's connector did not permit environment changes for this beta, so its verified public URL is versioned in source.

## Development and validation

From `main/ui/web`: `npm.cmd run desktop:dev`, `npm.cmd run build`, and `npm.cmd run desktop:check`. Rust tests: `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib`. The browser preview shows the interface but intentionally cannot start local inference; use the native application.

Backend tests: `NewAnubisTri/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -B -m pytest main/ui/api/tests/test_desktop_result.py main/ui/api/tests/test_security.py main/ui/api/tests/test_analysis.py main/ui/api/tests/test_parser_required_columns.py main/ui/api/tests/test_pipeline_child.py main/ui/api/tests/test_config.py -q -p no:cacheprovider`.

Known research limitations remain: demoparser2 0.41.4 stale user-command values, the saved sklearn calibration version warning, and no guarantee that calibrated estimates generalize to a particular match. The passing parser sentinel verifies the column contract, not the freshness of all input values. Those behaviors were not changed for desktop integration.

### Recorded local checks (2026-10-08)

- The six-file Python suite above passed: 62 tests, including API security, required-column rejection, report ordering/calibration, invalid/oversized local demos, and pipeline child failure behavior. The focused desktop/child subset passed again after watchdog changes (11 tests).
- Rust library tests passed: 3 tests covering SHA-256, refreshing changed cached models, and the external URL allowlist.
- The frozen API parent-watchdog test passed: closing the parent pipe stopped the service with the intended exit code 75 in 2.01 seconds.
- Closing the final native window stopped both of its owned backend processes. The app was then reopened without the validation-only browser debugging port.
- The full patch-14153 parser sentinel passed (1,089,620 tick rows). Decorative-field warnings and the existing sklearn calibration-version warning remain visible.
- Next.js and desktop production frontend builds passed. The active desktop JavaScript bundle is 178.37 kB (56.51 kB gzip); CSS is 6.65 kB (2.47 kB gzip).
- The real 232,415,622-byte sentinel demo completed through the source desktop API in 51.71 seconds and through the frozen backend in 56.29 seconds, each producing ten players. Player ranks and scores were exactly identical. These are single local observations under concurrent build activity, not a controlled benchmark or a general determinism guarantee. A missing frozen parser-version field discovered in the comparison was corrected by packaging its distribution metadata.
- The final native release application processed `TEST_20260501_102349_02b8afde.dem` through its drop handler and Analyze button, rendered ten real players in 82.45 seconds, and saved a 2,633-byte report through the Windows Save dialog. Its ranks and scores exactly matched the source run; parser provenance reported 0.41.4 and both research warnings were visible. No frontend errors were recorded. This also verified the corrected sidecar bootstrap order: the bundled module paths are established before importing the inference watchdog.
- The local NSIS installer built successfully (378,508,232 bytes), but is deliberately unsigned and unpublished. SHA-256: `90731012a1cf77a4c9ac0a93580cea6668677de2885e167e3dfb5f0755e01045`. It is a workstation test artifact, not an approved public release.

Public release remains gated on Windows and updater signing, an actual release feed, clean-machine installation testing, and an update from a previous signed version. This workstation has development tools installed, so its passing packaged run is not a substitute for a clean-machine test.

### Release review (2026-10-09)

**Release blocked: dependency advisories remain unresolved. Do not distribute the unsigned workstation candidate as an approved release.** The full installed Python environment audit reported advisory matches in ten packages: aiohttp 3.13.3, datasets 4.6.0, fsspec 2026.2.0, multidict 6.7.1, Pillow 12.1.0, pytest 9.0.2, requests 2.32.5, setuptools 81.0.0, torch 2.11.0, and urllib3 2.6.3. Its 102 advisory records include aliases/duplicates and tooling packages; this is not a finding that 102 distinct vulnerabilities are reachable through demo analysis. The PyTorch advisory is PYSEC-2025-194, with 2.13.0 listed as fixed. Do not upgrade that runtime in place: prepare a separate candidate environment, resolve advisories, rebuild, and validate model loading, calibration, parser contract, and real-demo parity before promoting it. No Python/model dependencies or research behavior were changed in this review.

The desktop production npm audit reported zero vulnerabilities. Cargo audit reported zero vulnerability entries but maintenance warnings for proc-macro-error and five unic crates, plus the glib soundness advisory RUSTSEC-2024-0429. Review target applicability and remediation; a zero vulnerability count is not a clean bill of health. Raw reports are local validation artifacts under `main/data/web_validation/desktop-{python,rust,audit}*`, not distributable application content.

Application fixes:

- Local demo requests now require a strict schema, local-drive paths, and server-generated job IDs. UNC/device paths, malformed payloads, and client-supplied IDs are rejected. Desktop server exceptions no longer return internal diagnostics.
- Queued status safely handles the period before a log exists. Log reads are bounded to the last 128 KiB. This fixes a reproduced HTTP 500 immediately after queuing a real demo.
- Starting a second analysis clears the previous job before polling begins. Frontend API/result requests have a 30-second timeout. OS reduced-motion changes are honored, and drag-handler registration failures provide a usable fallback message.
- Native engine startup is serialized to prevent concurrent IPC requests from launching duplicate sidecars. Generated resource cleanup excludes `.env*` and private-key/certificate filename extensions. This filename filter supplements the explicit payload allowlist; it is not a content-level secret scanner.

Current validation:

- `python -B -m pytest main/ui/api/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp main/data/web_validation/release-tests-final --tb=short`: **72 passed**, one FastAPI/httpx deprecation warning.
- `cargo test --manifest-path main/ui/web/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib`: **3 passed** after the startup serialization change.
- `python main/scripts/check_parser_contract.py`: passed the patch-14153 full parse, **1,089,620 rows**. Decorative-property and existing research limitations remain.
- Desktop frontend and native `npm run desktop:build -- --no-bundle` builds passed; packaged `check-runtime` passed. Current JavaScript: 178.71 kB, 56.60 kB gzip. This built an unsigned executable, not a new release installer; the October 8 installer above is stale relative to these fixes.
- A real 232,415,622-byte demo completed via the source desktop API in **74.40 s** and the rebuilt frozen API in **62.85 s**, each producing ten players and reporting Queued, Parsing, Feature processing, Temporal inference, Scoring, Results ready. These are individual local observations, not controlled performance benchmarks.
- Source and rebuilt frozen runs had exactly identical player IDs, ranks, model scores, review scores, and calibrated probabilities. All **61** packaged manifest hashes independently verified, with no prohibited secret filenames found.
- The rebuilt native app's actual drop-event handler and Analyze button produced and rendered ten players in **64.01 s**. Browser automation recorded no page errors and verified OS reduced-motion handling; the resulting native screenshot was inspected. This used a temporary loopback WebView debugging port for validation, not a shipped debugging setting.
- A second analysis in the same native session cleared the old results correctly and again rendered ten players. Exact ranks and numerical scores matched the source/frozen runs. This repeatability observation covers this demo and machine only.
- Targeted Windows Defender scans of both rebuilt executables completed (Operational events 1000/1001), with no detection event in the scan interval. Signatures were dated October 9. This does not establish reputation or behavior on other antivirus products; the native candidate remains `NotSigned`.
- The website production build and browser checks passed for all six rolling cards and mobile layout; desktop/mobile screenshots of the new temporal network were inspected. The graphic is explicitly conceptual and does not fabricate model activations.

Before publishing, also complete clean-machine install/uninstall, real signed update and tamper tests, supported Windows/WebView2 checks, and antivirus/reputation review of the final signed binaries. None of those is established by a successful developer-workstation run. Local artifact confidentiality, a hardened parser sandbox, automatic retention, and broad production capacity guarantees remain outside what this client currently provides.

### Security remediation (2026-10-10; supersedes the dependency blocker above)

An isolated Windows/Python 3.13 runtime now passes `pip check` and `pip-audit` with **no known vulnerabilities reported**. Exact versions, including build tools, are recorded in `main/ui/web/scripts/requirements-desktop.lock.txt` (95 packages). Security updates were limited to aiohttp 3.14.3, datasets 5.0.1, fsspec 2026.6.0, multidict 6.9.1, Pillow 12.3.0, pytest 9.0.3, requests 2.33.0, setuptools 83.0.0, torch 2.13.0, urllib3 2.8.0, and the new virtual environment's pip 26.2. These address the scanner findings, not feature requests. PyPI and the raw upstream PyTorch advisory differed on affected versions; the release candidate uses the PyPI-listed fixed version rather than suppressing the finding.

The existing research environment and worker requirements remain unchanged. Model weights, architectures, feature contracts, parser version, sklearn version, calibration, and ranking formulas remain unchanged. In the candidate environment all **72 backend tests passed**; the full patch-14153 sentinel passed; a real 232,415,622-byte demo produced ten players in **37.09 seconds** through the desktop API. Player identities, ranks, raw scores, calibrated probabilities, and review scores matched the original runtime exactly. This is evidence for the tested demo, not proof of parity on every possible input or a performance benchmark. An integration bootstrap bug was fixed: `run_infer_pipeline.py` no longer removes virtual-environment paths merely because their name contains `ClarityCS\main`.

The Windows Cargo dependency tree excludes `glib` and `proc-macro-error`, so those advisory warnings do not describe the Windows shipped runtime. The five `unic` maintenance warnings do apply transitively through Tauri's URL parser and remain tracked; no vulnerable code finding was reported by Cargo audit. No advisory suppression was added.

The website's compatible security updates removed all **production** npm audit findings (including the Next.js update to 16.4.0). Three Node tests, the production build, desktop/mobile browser checks, About navigation, and safe unavailable-download handling passed. Seven build/development graph findings remain through Tailwind 3 (`braces`/`postcss-selector-parser` and their dependents). Their input is repository-controlled build configuration/styles; do not run untrusted contributions on a release runner holding signing secrets. A Tailwind 4 migration is separate work; `npm audit fix --force` was deliberately not used. The website download validator now rejects nonstandard ports, credentials, queries, fragments, extra path segments, malformed escapes, encoded separators, and control characters.

Publication still requires a Windows code-signing certificate, Tauri update-signing credentials, the real release feed, and signed clean-machine installation/update testing. No code-signing certificate was found in the current-user or machine certificate stores. The website can be deployed with downloads disabled while these are arranged. Do not point its download setting at an unsigned local installer or push generated executables/model caches into Git. Respect the repository's documented unrelated public `main` history when preparing a reviewed publication branch.

Final October 10 artifacts and checks:

- Rebuilt frozen API: ten real players in **33.89 s**, exact score/rank parity with the original runtime; all 61 package hashes verified. Native app: ten players rendered in **54.03 s**, no recorded page errors. These are individual workstation observations under concurrent build activity.
- Frozen service rejects unauthenticated requests (401), UNC paths (400), client-injected job IDs (422), and nonexistent local files (400). Unavailable desktop results retain the existing 409 response contract. A deliberately corrupt replay failed with a high-level parser message in the native UI, removed old results, and allowed retry. Normal window close left no backend processes running.
- Direct local launch: `main/ui/web/src-tauri/target/release/nullcs-desktop.exe`. Keep its generated resource directories alongside it; the executable alone is not a portable distribution.
- Fresh local installer: `main/ui/web/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/NullCS_0.1.0-beta.1_x64-setup.exe`, **389,440,214 bytes**, SHA-256 `3fed147c979057e78ef0f25e8339caa656e8a8709faa828e5034c86f0bb2debc`. Authenticode status: **NotSigned**. Targeted Defender scan completed with no detection event observed in the scan interval. This supersedes the stale October 8 installer, but remains a local test candidate, not a public release.

To publish: prepare a scoped publication branch preserving the public repository history; deploy `main/ui/site` with its tested lockfile and the download unset; provision signing credentials/feed; run `build-signed-release.ps1` with the locked release interpreter; test that signed installer and update on a clean Windows machine; publish verified release assets; then set `NULLCS_DESKTOP_DOWNLOAD_URL` to that exact GitHub installer and rebuild/redeploy the website. No push, release publication, or deployment was performed in this review.

`METHODOLOGY.md`:

```md
# Methodology

NullCS looks at post-match telemetry. It never judges an account from one round or
one kill. It ranks players and moments worth a human look, and keeps enough
evidence to explain why a score moved.

## 1. Data

Two sources feed the current artifacts:

- parsed CS2 demos from the original player-level pipeline (demoparser/AWPy based);
- the CS2CD benchmark set, split into matches with and without a known cheater.

Verified sizes:

| Item | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Demos in the window-model data | 894 |
| Engagement windows | 281,792 |
| Demos in player evaluation (after the 8-player filter) | 860 |
| Player rows | 6,886 (992 positive / 5,894 negative) |

Labels are used to measure the research pipeline. They are not proof that every
elevated moment is cheating.

## 2. Engagement windows

A window is a short slice of ticks around one player-versus-player interaction.
Windows describe *process*, not only outcome:

- what the attacker could see, and when the target first became visible;
- how the aim moved before and after that moment;
- whether a shot or damage landed before the aim settled;
- how distance and movement changed;
- how mouse and view input behaved after the target was acquired.

## 3. Window model

A small temporal CNN reads fixed-length windows: 35 channels over 32 ticks. The
channels cover aim error, mouse delta, view/command gaps, distance and speed,
angular velocity and jerk, visibility state and transitions, movement state
(walking, airborne, scoped) and shot/damage timing.

The CNN scores windows only. Its scores are summarised per player (mean, top-k
mean, high-score rate and similar) and become inputs to the ranking model.

## 4. Player features

Per player and per demo the pipeline computes 449 features, in plain groups:

- **Counts:** kills, rounds, victims, weapons.
- **Reaction time:** typical value, spread, and how often it is very short.
- **Precision and habit:** headshot rate, through-smoke rate, prefire-like rate,
  long-range fast reactions, weapon mix.
- **Aim process:** how quickly aim settles, how noisy it stays, how it collapses
  onto the target.
- **Movement and context:** distance, speed, visibility exposure.
- **Window-model summaries.**

Identifiers such as SteamID and player name are never used as features.

## 5. Ranking model

Gradient-boosted trees over the 449 features, evaluated with grouped
cross-validation:

- groups are demo IDs, so a match never lands in both training and validation;
- class imbalance is handled with data-dependent weighting;
- the saved scores are isotonic-calibrated, which improves Brier score and log loss.

Calibrated or not, the output is a review priority, not a probability suitable for
enforcement.

## 6. Keeping ourselves honest

- **Grouped splits** by demo ID prevent same-match leakage.
- **Identifiers are excluded** from the feature set.
- **The feature list is locked** to a published 449-feature file, so a training run
  cannot silently change the contract, and the manifest records which file was used.
- **Training and inference share one aggregation implementation**, so served
  features cannot drift from trained features.
- **Known limit:** the split is match-isolated but not chronological. It measures
  generalisation across demos, not future drift.

## 7. How to read a score

| Score | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| High | Inspect this player first. |
| Medium | Check whether the evidence is concentrated or thin. |
| Low | The measured behaviour did not stand out. |

No single feature and no single score is a verdict.
```

`PIPELINE.md`:

```md
# Pipeline

Practical map for rebuilding the public artifacts. All paths are relative to the
repository root, and commands are meant to be run from there.

## Data flow

```text
raw demos
  -> parsed per-demo zips (parquet tables)
  -> engagement rows per demo
  -> encounter windows and window-model scores
  -> player-demo feature table
  -> grouped model training
  -> out-of-fold reports and ranked review output
```

## Commands

Parse, build features, aggregate, train, evaluate:

```powershell
python main/src/parse/parse_demos_awpy_api.py
python main/src/features/build_engagement_features.py
python main/src/features/aggregate_player_features.py
python main/scripts/train_xgb_gridcv.py
python main/scripts/evaluate_xgb_gridcv.py
```

Inference and explanation:

```powershell
python main/scripts/run_infer_pipeline.py --dem_path path\to\match.dem
python main/scripts/explain_demo.py --demo CDemo3
python main/scripts/explain_demo.py --demo CDemo3 --steamid 76561198762460140
```

`run_infer_pipeline.py` is the full inference path (it also scores encounter windows).

## Key artifacts

| Artifact | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `main/data/processed/demos/<demo_id>/engagement_features.parquet` | one row per engagement |
| `main/data/processed/player_features_cs2cd.parquet` | player-demo feature table |
| `main/data/processed/models/xgb_player_level_cs2cd.json` | model used by inference (pinned) |
| `main/data/processed/models/xgb_player_level_cs2cd_features.txt` | the 449-feature contract |
| `main/data/processed/models/xgb_player_level_cs2cd_eval_summary.json` | saved evaluation summary |
| `main/data/processed/models/encounter_nn_cs2cd_training_manifest.json` | window-model summary |
| `main/data/processed/reports/encounter_nn_cs2cd_oof_encounters.parquet` | window scores, out-of-fold |
| `main/data/processed/reports/ranked_player_demo_suspicion_oof_cs2cd.csv` | ranked players plus evidence |
| `main/data/processed/reports/ranked_demo_suspicion_oof_cs2cd.csv` | ranked demos, top-k summary |

## House rules worth knowing

- Inference loads the pinned artifact (`xgb_player_level_cs2cd`). Point it elsewhere
  with `--model-artifact`, `NULLCS_MODEL_ARTIFACT` or `NULLCS_DEFAULT_MODEL_STEM`.
- Training locks the feature list to the mode contract by default. Use
  `--feature-list-path` to pin a different list, or `--no-feature-list-lock` for the
  old auto-select behaviour.
- `GroupKFold` groups by `demo_id`. It is not a chronological split.
- Evaluation retrains fold models to produce out-of-fold numbers; only inference
  loads a saved model.
- Some older scripts still use hardcoded absolute paths.
```

`PRODUCTION_INTEGRATION.md`:

```md
# NullCS website inference integration

> Product update (2026-10-08): the website `/analyze` entry now points to the downloadable local client. The hosted inference implementation below is retained but is not the primary public workflow. See [DESKTOP_RELEASE.md](DESKTOP_RELEASE.md) for the active desktop architecture and release gates.

The repository implements live analysis at `/analyze`. No production Python host has been provisioned. The Vercel website needs a separately deployed, persistent Python worker before live production analysis can operate. Missing gateway configuration produces an explicit unavailable message; the existing research pages remain usable.

## Architecture and ownership

1. The browser sends only `{filename, size}` to the Next.js `/api/analysis` gateway. It establishes a signed, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict browser ownership cookie (30-day expiry).
2. Next.js authenticates to FastAPI using a server-only shared key and the verified owner ID. FastAPI persists a server-generated job ID and a hashed, expiring, single-use upload capability in SQLite.
3. The browser streams the `.dem` directly to the worker's HTTPS `PUT /api/analysis/{job}/upload`, using the capability in its Authorization header. Demo bytes never pass through a Vercel function. No Supabase service or storage credentials are required by this implementation.
4. The worker writes private `.partial` storage, checks actual length and CS2 header, hashes the upload, atomically renames it, and queues the job. Default maximum is 1 GiB. Client filenames are display metadata only; clients cannot choose storage keys or filesystem paths.
5. A single executor invokes the existing research CLI and persists a public result snapshot. Next.js proxies only allowlisted, owned status/results/explanation/evidence JSON. Model inference runs outside HTTP handlers.

This is anonymous **browser-session ownership**, not account authentication. Another browser cannot enumerate or retrieve the job by knowing its ID. Losing/expiring the cookie loses access; there is no cross-device recovery. Before broad public release, decide whether account authentication, operator admission, and/or additional ingress abuse controls are required. CORS is only a browser restriction; the gateway key and job capability enforce backend authorization.

## Canonical boundary and research integrity

`main/ui/api/pipeline_runtime.py::inference_command` launches `main/scripts/run_infer_pipeline.py --dem_path <server path> --demo_id <server ID> --out_dir <dedicated processed root>`, with the existing optional model override. `pipeline_child.py` supervises parent lifetime and runs that same entry point. Both `NULLCS_UPLOAD_DIR` and `CLARITY_PROCESSED_DIR` are passed to child processes so temporal lookup uses the same data tree.

The CLI changes are four explicit stage log messages. Feature definitions/order/hash, the 449-feature contract, aggregation, encounters/windows, temporal construction, model weights/selection, calibration, thresholds, and research scoring remain unchanged. No models were retrained and no LLM was added. Production follows the canonical CSV's risk ranking, including its tie order; it does not apply the legacy desktop API's additional display reordering. Existing interpretation/evidence functions are reused.

Each job loads models through the existing CLI. The parser still runs for both initial features and temporal loading. No speculative model cache, parser optimization, or dependency upgrade was introduced. The worker rejects the stale generated desktop executable as a production runtime.

Backend `.env` files now load before shared path constants are imported, so evidence loaders and the worker agree on configured storage roots. This integration fix does not change feature or model behavior.

## Lifecycle, failures, and persistence

| State/stage | Actual trigger |
|---|---|
| `upload_pending` | Durable reservation created |
| `uploading` | Valid capability atomically claimed |
| `queued` | Entire replay validated and saved |
| `running / preparing` | Executor starts the research process |
| `parsing` | CLI enters demoparser2 loading |
| `feature_processing` | Parsed tables are available; feature construction starts |
| `inference` | Temporal model feature step starts |
| `scoring` | Player scoring starts |
| `results_ready` | CLI exits successfully and structured results are published |
| `failed` | Upload, parsing, model, feature, scoring, publication, timeout, or interruption failure |

Only upload byte transfer has a percentage. Analysis stages come from explicit events, never elapsed-time estimates. Explanation state is separate: `unavailable -> queued -> running -> ready/failed`. The explanation CLI is `main/scripts/explain_demo.py --demo <job> --steamid <player> --mode infer`. Failed explanations do not remove ranked results and may be retried.

SQLite stores owners, jobs, upload-ticket hashes, events, and explanation states. Artifacts remain in private storage; public snapshots are `reports/<job>/web_result.json` and `<steamid>/web_explanation.json`. Atomic snapshot replacement prevents partially written JSON from appearing ready. The single process lock and serial executor protect the canonical global ranking CSV's read/rewrite behavior. **Run exactly one worker process/replica per data directory; never run research CLIs against that directory concurrently.**

Startup marks interrupted uploads/inference/explanations failed; queued work survives restart. The parent pipe watchdog terminates orphan research children. CLI timeouts kill the child. Pending reservations expire. Upload failure removes partial data where the filesystem permits it. Completed and failed analysis artifacts are retained for diagnosis; no automatic retention period or user deletion policy has been invented. Monitor disk use, back up SQLite and artifacts consistently, and define retention before public operation. The free-space floor is an admission guard, not a proof that every demo's intermediate files fit.

## Public contract

Schema version: `nullcs.analysis.v1`. Status includes job ID, stage/state, demo filename, event timestamps, measured runtime and safe error code/message. Results include:

- Demo filename/size/map and parser provenance.
- Canonical ranked players, string Steam IDs/names, `rank`, raw `model_score`, nullable `calibrated_probability`, existing adjusted `risk`, evidence confidence and feature/interpretation summaries.
- Per-player explanation state, warnings, model artifact basename and SHA-256/feature-list hash.
- Separate generated explanations and allowlisted evidence tables (first 2,000 rows; explicit truncation indicator).

Calibrated probability is `null` when the selected model lacks its own calibrator. No replacement calibration is manufactured. Internal paths, raw feature debug traces, private logs, owner IDs, ticket hashes and shared secrets are not returned. Player names and metadata render as React text. Raw parser/model diagnostics remain in worker logs.

The gateway supports reservation/capabilities, `{job}/status`, `{job}/results`, and `{job}/players/{steamid}/{explain,explanation,evidence/<filename>}` only. It cannot proxy arbitrary backend paths or uploads. POST requests require the exact website Origin. The worker disables legacy demo-list/upload/result routes in website mode to prevent bypassing ownership checks.

## Deployment

Keep Next.js on Vercel (`main/ui/site`). Deploy FastAPI on a separately managed host/container with HTTPS ingress, persistent local disk, and Python **3.13** (validated locally on 3.13.5). Install `main/ui/api/requirements-worker.txt`, preserving existing pins; its only additional explicit dependency is `joblib==1.5.3`, already used by the saved artifact loaders and present in the validated environment.

The measured local inference runtime uses CPU PyTorch. GPU is not required for functionality. Production CPU throughput, memory capacity, concurrency and hosting limits must be measured on the chosen host. Use one executor initially. SQLite WAL and the output lock require a local filesystem with working locking; do not place this data tree on an untested network filesystem.

Provision a private persistent directory with `uploads/`, `processed/` and `state/`. Copy the selected model bundle to `processed/models/`, preserving its artifact names. For the verified default bundle:

```text
xgb_player_level_cs2cd.json
xgb_player_level_cs2cd_features.txt
xgb_player_level_cs2cd_training_manifest.json
xgb_player_level_cs2cd_calibration.pkl
encounter_nn_cs2cd.pt
encounter_nn_cs2cd_features.json
encounter_nn_cs2cd_preproc.pkl
encounter_nn_cs2cd_training_manifest.json
```

Preserve the corresponding bundle/manifest if intentionally selecting a rank variant or other supported override; a rank-selected model may legitimately have no calibrator. Do not substitute the absent `encounter_nn_cs2cd_temporal_seq32.pt`. Model artifacts are not embedded in the image or committed by this change.

Native startup, from the repository root with worker variables set:

```sh
python -m pip install -r main/ui/api/requirements-worker.txt
python -m uvicorn main.ui.api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --workers 1 --no-proxy-headers --timeout-graceful-shutdown 15
```

Container build definition: `main/ui/api/Dockerfile.worker` (not the pre-existing demo-mode root Dockerfile/Compose setup). Build from the repository root:

```sh
docker build -f main/ui/api/Dockerfile.worker -t nullcs-worker .
```

Mount the dedicated persistent volume at `/data`, writable by UID 10001. The image runs without root, includes `libgomp1`, excludes unrelated repository/data/secrets from its build context, and supplies the packaged root marker required by existing path resolution. Supply the key and exact frontend origin at runtime. Prefer a read-only model bind mount at `/data/processed/models`. Do not expose the data volume as static files.

Health check: authenticated `GET /api/health`; check `upload_enabled`. It confirms executor availability, not model correctness or throughput. Perform the real demo acceptance check below before routing public traffic. Terminate HTTPS at the chosen ingress and forward to port 8000. Allow a 1 GiB request and at least the configured upload duration, with streaming/request buffering configured appropriately. Next.js must be able to reach the worker control API; browsers must reach its public upload URL. Configure CORS for `https://www.nullcs.app`. No production hostname has been invented or provisioned.

## Environment variables

Templates: `main/ui/site/.env.example` and `main/ui/api/.env.example`. Generate independent random secrets of at least 32 characters; never commit values.

| Variable | Component / exposure | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `NULLCS_API_BASE_URL` | Next.js server only | Worker origin for small control requests |
| `NULLCS_WORKER_PUBLIC_URL` | Next.js config; returned URL is public | Browser-reachable HTTPS worker origin; defaults to API origin |
| `NULLCS_API_KEY` | Next.js + worker; secret | Shared gateway authentication |
| `NULLCS_SESSION_SECRET` | Next.js server only; secret | Signs browser ownership cookies; rotation invalidates sessions |
| `NULLCS_WEB_ANALYSIS=1` | Worker only | Enables private website jobs and disables legacy routes |
| `NULLCS_ENV=production` | Worker only | Production error/auth behavior |
| `NULLCS_DEMO_MODE=0` | Worker only | Required for real inference |
| `NULLCS_FRONTEND_ORIGIN` | Worker config; public origin | Exact allowed website origin |
| `NULLCS_UPLOAD_DIR` | Worker only | Dedicated private upload volume |
| `CLARITY_PROCESSED_DIR` | Worker only | Dedicated artifacts/models/reports volume; research default is rejected |
| `NULLCS_WEB_STATE_DIR` | Worker only | SQLite state; default sibling `web_state` |
| `NULLCS_PROJECT_ROOT`, `CLARITY_PYTHON_EXE` | Worker only | Optional explicit repository/runtime locations |
| `NULLCS_MODEL_ARTIFACT` / `CLARITY_MODEL_ARTIFACT` | Worker only | Existing optional model override |
| `NULLCS_WEB_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | Worker config; limit public | Default 1073741824 bytes |
| `NULLCS_WEB_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Worker only | Upload/reservation lifetime; default 1800 |
| `NULLCS_WEB_MAX_PENDING_JOBS` | Worker only | Global pending cap, default 8; also two active jobs per owner |
| `NULLCS_WEB_MIN_FREE_BYTES` | Worker only | Default 2147483648-byte free-space floor |
| `NULLCS_JOB_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Worker only | Inference timeout, default 1800 |
| `NULLCS_EXPLAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Worker only | Explanation timeout, default 120 |
| `NULLCS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Worker only | Small control request timeout, default 30 |
| `NULLCS_RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY`, `NULLCS_RATE_LIMIT_REFILL_PER_SECOND` | Worker only | Request token bucket, defaults 30 and 0.5 |

All analysis secrets lack the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix. Existing `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_*` placeholders are unused by this flow. No service-role credential belongs in the browser. Locally, use site `http://localhost:3001`, API/public worker `http://127.0.0.1:8001`, and matching worker CORS. Use HTTPS origins in production. `.env.example` is a template, not a source of live credentials.

## Validation and release gate

```sh
python -B -m pytest main/ui/api/tests/test_config.py main/ui/api/tests/test_security.py main/ui/api/tests/test_analysis.py main/ui/api/tests/test_parser_required_columns.py main/ui/api/tests/test_pipeline_child.py -q -p no:cacheprovider

# In main/ui/site:
node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/analysis-security.test.mjs
npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false
npm run build
```

The HTTP acceptance script uses the real website gateway, direct upload, canonical models, persistence, access-control checks, separate explanations, and actual evidence. It compares repeat ranked outputs and provenance without seeding/changing research behavior. Browser verification additionally checks rendered player/evidence tables. Keep reports/screenshots/demo copies in ignored private storage.

Linux CPython 3.13 wheel metadata resolution passed for the pinned requirements using pip's cross-platform dry run. This is **not** a built-container test: Windows-host environment markers can differ from Linux, and CUDA-related dependencies/native libraries must still be checked inside the image. Docker is unavailable in the validation environment. Before deployment, build the image, load both model artifacts/calibrator, run the parser sentinel and a real demo inside it, then measure resource usage and verify volume/restart/HTTPS ingress behavior.

### Observed local results (2026-10-06)

- 50 Python tests passed: the existing four security tests, 22 required-column rejection cases, transport/ownership/failure/lifecycle checks, real missing-model CLI failure, model-import and parent-death watchdog checks, and environment-file path consistency. Only the existing Starlette/httpx deprecation warning appeared.
- Both Node gateway security tests passed. TypeScript and the optimized Next.js production build passed. Browser bundles contained neither local validation secret.
- The patch-14153 sentinel passed its full production guard: 1,089,620 tick rows, with the same two decorative-field warnings.
- Real `TEST_20260501_102349_02b8afde.dem` (232,415,622 bytes; de_inferno) entered through the browser, uploaded directly to port 8001, ran the canonical models, persisted results, and displayed all ten ranked players. Separate explanations produced four tables; the top player's reaction-time table had 20 rows and smoke table three rows (two other tables legitimately empty). Browser console checks found no errors.
- Two fresh complete HTTP runs through Next.js and the worker had exactly equal player ordering, raw/calibrated/review scores, confidence, model hashes, and parser provenance. This establishes repeatability for that fixture/runtime, not universal determinism across hardware or parser versions.
- Measured inference times were 38.25 and 35.46 seconds for those two runs; complete HTTP checks including upload/polling/explanation/evidence took 46.59 and 43.02 seconds. The final browser run took 34.9 seconds for inference; an earlier browser run took 50.6 seconds. These are local observations, not before/after optimization claims or production capacity estimates.
- On the local i5-13400F / approximately 32 GiB Windows machine with CPU PyTorch, a sampled inference process reported a peak working set of 2,073,485,312 bytes (approximately 1.93 GiB). This is not a recommended memory limit or a worst-case bound for larger demos.
- A valid-header but corrupt 32-byte demo failed through the real website/API path with `parser_failed`, without exposing a traceback/path. An interrupted job became `worker_restarted` on startup. Upload cleanup errors, process timeout, duplicate capabilities, capacity, unauthorized access, and fair explanation scheduling have focused tests.
- After restarting the worker, the browser's existing owner session still retrieved all ten persisted players and a `ready` explanation. The existing homepage also loaded without browser errors.
- The real `xgb_player_level_cs2cd_ranksel_base` model scored the fixture's actual extracted features into ten players with all calibrated probabilities absent. The normal model/calibrator loaded through every complete run and retained its version warning.
- The XGBoost hash remains `f9016d95a144e1004f40c01f15b86879d9d9101cdda4659acaa261ac80610ea8`; the 449-feature-list hash remains `26dfc64615695c1bac225b37eb42cd0efa72a0247c4af685b64da29ae42a58e4`.

Private reproducibility artifacts are under ignored `main/data/web_validation/` (HTTP report, parser check, logs, snapshots, screenshots, memory samples and wheel metadata). They must not be committed or exposed as static content.

### Reliability follow-up (2026-10-07)

Review of the existing tree found one explanation recovery gap: a lost or corrupt completed explanation snapshot left its state at `ready`, preventing regeneration. The owned explanation endpoint now records `failed`, returns a safe retryable error, and preserves ranked results. Three additional cases cover missing/corrupt snapshots and actual explanation CLI failure with absent inputs. `python -B -m pytest main/ui/api/tests/test_analysis.py main/ui/api/tests/test_security.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` passed all **28 targeted tests**. The previous successful full-pipeline runs were retained, not repeated. Production hosting and actual container execution remain external blockers.

## Remaining known limitations

- `demoparser2==0.41.4` has the upstream stale user-command issue (LaihoE/demoparser issue 340). The passing patch-14153 schema sentinel cannot prove those values are semantically fresh. No speculative parser change was made.
- The saved sklearn calibrator emits its existing 1.7.1-to-1.9.0 serialization warning. Artifact behavior is preserved and the UI warns; rank variants without calibration remain explicitly uncalibrated.
- Existing explanation reason summaries may use different evidence subsets from the scoring signal values. They are exposed as the existing research explanations; no feature/formula reconciliation was silently performed.
- Historical paths, the stale desktop executable, and unrelated audit issues remain outside this integration. The new worker uses dedicated configured paths and the Python CLI.
- Retention/deletion policy, account requirements, public abuse protection, production capacity, actual container execution, and production HTTPS deployment remain operator decisions/acceptance checks.

The future investigation/agent integration point is the owned `nullcs.analysis.v1` result plus per-player explanation/evidence endpoints. An agent can consume that evidence later without entering or changing the classification/ranking path. No agent layer is implemented.

`README.md`:

```md
# NullCS

## Community desktop beta

Download the Windows x64 installer from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/gjones01/NullCS/releases). This beta is unsigned; Windows may show an unknown-publisher warning. Do not disable security protections. Automatic updates are not configured yet: check Releases for new versions.

Analyze a local CS2 `.dem` up to 1 GiB, review the ranked players, and save a plain-text report. Processing stays on your computer. Scores are research signals, not cheating verdicts. Read [release/setup requirements](DESKTOP_RELEASE.md) and [attributions](NOTICE.md).

Original NullCS code and original model artifacts are GPL-3.0-only; third-party materials retain their own licenses. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Contributions submitted for inclusion must be available under this license; contributors retain their copyrights.

To build the desktop app, use Windows x64/Python 3.13, install `main/ui/web/scripts/requirements-desktop.lock.txt` in a fresh environment, and set `NULLCS_RELEASE_PYTHON` to its Python executable. Download the matching `nullcs-model-artifacts.zip` release asset, verify it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and extract its contents into `main/data/processed/models/`. Install the web dependencies with `npm ci` in `main/ui/web`, then run `npm run desktop:build`. The installer does not require an installed Python runtime. Building also requires Rust and the Windows desktop build tools documented in DESKTOP_RELEASE.md.

NullCS reads Counter-Strike 2 demo files and turns them into a ranked list of
players worth a human look, together with the measurements that pushed each score
up.

It is **not** an anti-cheat, **not** a ban system and **not** an automatic verdict.
A high score means "look here first". Nothing more.

## The question

Scoreboard numbers are too coarse. A high headshot rate or a very short reaction
time can be meaningful, but skill, weapon choice, angle, visibility and round
context all move those numbers too. NullCS asks a narrower question:

> Can tick-level demo data surface unusual behaviour for review, while staying
> quiet on legitimate high-skill play?

## How it works

```text
CS2 .dem file
  -> per-tick parse tables
  -> short windows around each engagement
  -> window model (what aim, mouse and visibility did before the shot)
  -> per-player match features (~450 numbers per player)
  -> ranking model
  -> ranked players plus the evidence rows behind each score
```

Two models, deliberately separate:

1. **Window model (CNN).** Reads short tick sequences around a fight: aim error,
   mouse movement, view/command gaps, visibility, movement, shot timing. It scores
   windows, never players.
2. **Ranking model (XGBoost).** Uses ~450 per-player numbers, including summaries
   of the window scores, to rank the players inside one demo.

## Current benchmark

Read from the saved evaluation artifacts (see [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md)):

| Metric | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Demos evaluated | 860 |
| Player rows (992 positive / 5,894 negative) | 6,886 |
| ROC-AUC | 0.956 |
| PR-AUC | 0.796 |
| Suspicious player ranked #1 in the lobby | 92.8% |
| Suspicious player ranked top-3 | 97.3% |

These are review-ranking numbers, not enforcement numbers.

## What it tends to find

- Suspicious rows rarely hinge on one event. They show clusters of high-scoring
  engagement windows.
- Fast rifle timing, prefire-like fights and headshot concentration separate some
  positive rows from the baseline.
- Some non-cheater matches still score high, usually high-headshot, fast-reaction
  games. That is expected, and it is only useful if it stays visible and checkable.

## Documentation

- [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md) - how the data and models are built, in plain language.
- [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md) - current numbers, what they mean, where it fails.
- [PIPELINE.md](PIPELINE.md) - commands to rebuild everything and where files land.

## Scope

This repository holds research code, documentation and the public site. It does not
ship raw demos, private match data, secrets or enforcement tooling.

## Credits and licence

Built on [`demoparser2`](https://github.com/LaihoE/demoparser) by LaihoE and
contributors. No open-source licence is granted; the documentation is public for
review and transparency.
```

`RESULTS.md`:

```md
# Results

Current public readout, taken from the saved artifacts under `main/data/processed`.
Nothing here is invented: each number is read from a file that is in the repository.

## What was measured

| | Window model | Ranking model |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Demos | 894 | 860 |
| Rows | 281,792 windows | 6,886 player rows |
| Positives / negatives | 30,559 / 251,233 | 992 / 5,894 |
| Features | 35 channels x 32 ticks | 449 |
| PR-AUC | 0.566 | 0.796 |
| ROC-AUC | 0.853 | 0.956 |
| Split | out-of-fold | GroupKFold by `demo_id` |

The window model is a feature generator; its scores become player-level summaries
rather than final verdicts.

### Threshold behaviour (ranking model, saved summary)

| Threshold | Precision | Recall |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.20 | 0.627 | 0.911 |
| 0.30 | 0.673 | 0.883 |
| 0.40 | 0.710 | 0.872 |
| 0.50 | 0.734 | 0.855 |

## Ranking, which is what review cares about

Across the 293 demos that contain a labelled suspicious player:

| Check | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Suspicious player ranked #1 | 92.8% |
| Suspicious player ranked #2 | 96.2% |
| Suspicious player ranked #3 | 97.3% |

The useful question is not only "can the model separate rows", but "does the player
a reviewer should open land near the top of that lobby". Most of the time, it does.

## What the data shows

**1. Player scores built from the window model separate the two groups.**
Median `enn_score_mean` is 0.774 for positive rows against 0.316 for negative rows,
and median `enn_high_rate` is 0.819 against 0.111. Suspicious rows tend to contain
clusters of high-scoring windows rather than one isolated event.

**2. The window model itself is doing real work.**
Median window score is 0.769 for positive windows against 0.188 for negative
windows. 35.2% of positive windows score at or above 0.90, against 1.2% of negative
windows.

**3. Fast rifle timing, prefire-like fights and headshots carry part of the signal.**
`prefire_rate_rifle` has a feature AUC of 0.826 (median 0.500 positive vs 0.111
negative), `rifle_fast_rt_rate` 0.811 (0.500 vs 0.158) and `headshot_rate` 0.808
(0.727 vs 0.462). None of them is sufficient on its own.

**4. Some process features separate by being lower, not higher.**
Positive rows show *less* pre-shot aim noise than negative rows
(`enc_preshot_err_std_mean` median 0.632 vs 1.129) and less noisy correction
(`enc_aim_collapse_ratio_high_rate` median 0.635 vs 0.778). Clean stabilisation can
be a signal in its own right.

## Where it gets things wrong

- **Legitimate players can score high.** Among 567 demos with no known cheater, the
  median top player score is 0.052, but the 90th percentile reaches 0.748 and some
  matches top out at 1.000. 221 negative rows from 92 clean demos reach a risk of
  0.50 or more. These are usually high-headshot, fast-reaction games with enough
  kills to support the statistics.
- **The top of the lobby can be wrong.** In 21 labelled-cheater demos the known
  suspicious player is not ranked first, sometimes clearly behind another player.
- **Known hard cases:** very high-skill play that looks efficient; players with too
  few supported fights to be stable; behaviour that leaves no measurable aim,
  timing or visibility trace; and anything outside the demo file, such as comms,
  team plans or multi-match history.

## What is not measured here

The artifacts support feature distributions, ranking metrics and score separation.
They do not support claims like "X% of confirmed cheater windows show a specific
correction pattern". Cheat-type-specific claims need dedicated labels first.

## A note on reproducibility

The saved summary is the reference for the numbers above. Re-running evaluation
today reproduces the ranking closely but not always to the last decimal
(0.793/0.956 rather than 0.796/0.956) with bit-identical inference, which points at
library-version drift rather than a model change. Pinned dependencies are tracked as
open work before any number here is treated as a regression target.
```

`main/scripts/analyze_cheater_misses.py`:

```py
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from xgboost import DMatrix, XGBClassifier


PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT))

from src.utils.demo_labels import load_cheater_map
from src.utils.project_paths import DEMOS_ROOT, MODELS_ROOT, PROCESSED_ROOT, REPORTS_ROOT
from src.utils.training_mode import model_artifact_paths


CHEATER_CSV = PROCESSED_ROOT / "CheaterSteamIDs.csv"


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Analyze cheater benchmark misses by comparing the top-ranked player against the labeled cheater row.")
    ap.add_argument("--benchmark-prefix", default="BENCH", help="Benchmark report/demo prefix to inspect, e.g. BENCH or PRUNE2.")
    ap.add_argument("--model-artifact", default=None, help="Optional model artifact filename. Defaults to current CS2CD artifact.")
    ap.add_argument("--top-deltas", type=int, default=12, help="How many contribution deltas to show per miss.")
    ap.add_argument("--top-summary", type=int, default=20, help="How many aggregate feature deltas to summarize.")
    return ap.parse_args()


def _default_model_artifact() -> str:
    return model_artifact_paths(MODELS_ROOT, "cs2cd")["model"].name


def _source_stem_from_demo_id(demo_id: str, prefix: str) -> str:
    stem = str(demo_id)
    expect = f"{prefix.upper()}_CHEATER_"
    if stem.upper().startswith(expect):
        return stem[len(expect) :]
    return stem


def _cheater_key_for_stem(stem: str) -> str:
    if stem.lower().startswith("demo"):
        return f"CDemo{stem[4:]}"
    return stem


def _load_feature_list(model_artifact_name: str) -> list[str]:
    if model_artifact_name.endswith(".json"):
        stem = model_artifact_name[:-5]
    else:
        stem = model_artifact_name
    feats_path = MODELS_ROOT / f"{stem}_features.txt"
    if not feats_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing feature list: {feats_path}")
    return [line.strip() for line in feats_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]


def _load_model(model_artifact_name: str) -> XGBClassifier:
    model_path = MODELS_ROOT / model_artifact_name
    if not model_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing model artifact: {model_path}")
    model = XGBClassifier()
    model.load_model(str(model_path))
    return model


def _ranked_sort_column(df: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    for col in ("risk", "proba_calibrated", "proba_cheater_infer"):
        if col in df.columns:
            return col
    raise ValueError("Could not find a score column in ranked inference CSV.")


def _iter_benchmark_demo_ids(prefix: str) -> list[str]:
    pattern = f"{prefix.upper()}_CHEATER_*"
    ids = sorted(
        [p.name for p in REPORTS_ROOT.glob(pattern) if p.is_dir()],
        key=lambda x: (
            int(re.search(r"(\d+)$", x).group(1)) if re.search(r"(\d+)$", x) else 10**9,
            x.lower(),
        ),
    )
    if not ids:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No benchmark report directories found for prefix {prefix!r}.")
    return ids


def _contrib_frame(model: XGBClassifier, features: pd.DataFrame, feature_names: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    matrix = DMatrix(features[feature_names], feature_names=feature_names)
    contribs = model.get_booster().predict(matrix, pred_contribs=True)
    cols = feature_names + ["bias"]
    return pd.DataFrame(contribs, columns=cols, index=features.index)


def main() -> int:
    args = parse_args()
    prefix = str(args.benchmark_prefix).strip().upper()
    model_artifact_name = str(args.model_artifact or _default_model_artifact()).strip()

    cheater_map = load_cheater_map(CHEATER_CSV)
    feature_names = _load_feature_list(model_artifact_name)
    model = _load_model(model_artifact_name)

    miss_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    aggregate_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    for demo_id in _iter_benchmark_demo_ids(prefix):
        ranked_path = REPORTS_ROOT / demo_id / "ranked_players_infer.csv"
        features_path = DEMOS_ROOT / demo_id / "player_features_infer.parquet"
        if not ranked_path.exists() or not features_path.exists():
            continue

        ranked = pd.read_csv(ranked_path, dtype={"attacker_steamid": str})
        score_col = _ranked_sort_column(ranked)
        ranked["attacker_steamid"] = ranked["attacker_steamid"].astype(str).str.strip()
        ranked = ranked.sort_values(score_col, ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
        ranked["rank"] = ranked.index + 1

        source_stem = _source_stem_from_demo_id(demo_id, prefix)
        cheater_ids = sorted(cheater_map.get(_cheater_key_for_stem(source_stem), set()))
        if not cheater_ids:
            continue

        cheater_rows = ranked[ranked["attacker_steamid"].isin(cheater_ids)].copy()
        if cheater_rows.empty:
            continue
        cheater_best = cheater_rows.sort_values("rank", ascending=True).iloc[0]
        if int(cheater_best["rank"]) <= 1:
            continue

        top_row = ranked.iloc[0]
        all_features = pd.read_parquet(features_path)
        all_features["attacker_steamid"] = all_features["attacker_steamid"].astype(str).str.strip()
        all_features = all_features.set_index("attacker_steamid", drop=False)
        compare_ids = [str(top_row["attacker_steamid"]), str(cheater_best["attacker_steamid"])]
        if any(sid not in all_features.index for sid in compare_ids):
            continue

        compare = all_features.loc[compare_ids].copy()
        contribs = _contrib_frame(model, compare, feature_names)
        top_sid = str(top_row["attacker_steamid"])
        cheater_sid = str(cheater_best["attacker_steamid"])
        delta = contribs.loc[top_sid, feature_names] - contribs.loc[cheater_sid, feature_names]
        value_delta = compare.loc[top_sid, feature_names] - compare.loc[cheater_sid, feature_names]
        delta_df = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "feature": feature_names,
                "contrib_delta_top_minus_cheater": delta.values,
                "value_delta_top_minus_cheater": value_delta.values,
                "top_value": compare.loc[top_sid, feature_names].values,
                "cheater_value": compare.loc[cheater_sid, feature_names].values,
            }
        ).sort_values("contrib_delta_top_minus_cheater", ascending=False)

        top_helping = delta_df.head(args.top_deltas).to_dict(orient="records")
        cheater_helping = delta_df.tail(args.top_deltas).sort_values("contrib_delta_top_minus_cheater", ascending=True).to_dict(orient="records")

        miss_rows.append(
            {
                "demo_id": demo_id,
                "source_demo": source_stem,
                "top_name": str(top_row.get("attacker_name", "")),
                "top_steamid": top_sid,
                "top_score": float(top_row[score_col]),
                "cheater_name": str(cheater_best.get("attacker_name", "")),
                "cheater_steamid": cheater_sid,
                "cheater_rank": int(cheater_best["rank"]),
                "cheater_score": float(cheater_best[score_col]),
                "score_gap": float(top_row[score_col] - cheater_best[score_col]),
                "top_helping_features": top_helping,
                "cheater_helping_features": cheater_helping,
            }
        )

        aggregate_rows.extend(
            {
                "demo_id": demo_id,
                "feature": row["feature"],
                "contrib_delta_top_minus_cheater": float(row["contrib_delta_top_minus_cheater"]),
                "abs_contrib_delta": abs(float(row["contrib_delta_top_minus_cheater"])),
                "value_delta_top_minus_cheater": float(row["value_delta_top_minus_cheater"]),
            }
            for row in delta_df.to_dict(orient="records")
        )

    if not miss_rows:
        raise RuntimeError("No cheater misses found for the requested benchmark prefix.")

    agg_df = pd.DataFrame(aggregate_rows)
    summary = (
        agg_df.groupby("feature", as_index=False)
        .agg(
            demos=("demo_id", "nunique"),
            mean_contrib_delta=("contrib_delta_top_minus_cheater", "mean"),
            median_contrib_delta=("contrib_delta_top_minus_cheater", "median"),
            mean_abs_contrib_delta=("abs_contrib_delta", "mean"),
            mean_value_delta=("value_delta_top_minus_cheater", "mean"),
        )
        .sort_values(["mean_contrib_delta", "mean_abs_contrib_delta"], ascending=[False, False])
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

    out_dir = REPORTS_ROOT / f"miss_analysis_{prefix.lower()}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    miss_json = out_dir / "cheater_miss_details.json"
    miss_json.write_text(json.dumps(miss_rows, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    summary_csv = out_dir / "feature_delta_summary.csv"
    summary.to_csv(summary_csv, index=False)

    top_summary = summary.head(args.top_summary)
    payload = {
        "created_at": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "benchmark_prefix": prefix,
        "model_artifact": model_artifact_name,
        "miss_count": len(miss_rows),
        "mean_cheater_rank_across_misses": float(pd.DataFrame(miss_rows)["cheater_rank"].mean()),
        "mean_score_gap_across_misses": float(pd.DataFrame(miss_rows)["score_gap"].mean()),
        "top_features_helping_wrong_player": top_summary.to_dict(orient="records"),
        "detail_json": str(miss_json),
        "summary_csv": str(summary_csv),
    }
    summary_json = out_dir / "miss_analysis_summary.json"
    summary_json.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"[OK] wrote {miss_json}")
    print(f"[OK] wrote {summary_csv}")
    print(f"[OK] wrote {summary_json}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

`main/scripts/analyze_feature_separation.py`:

```py
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score


PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT))

from src.utils.project_paths import PROCESSED_ROOT, REPORTS_ROOT
from src.utils.scoring import ensure_no_forbidden_features
from src.utils.training_mode import player_features_path, resolve_train_data_mode


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Analyze feature separation for cheater vs non-cheater labels.")
    ap.add_argument("--train-data", default=None, help="Training data mode: local, cs2cd, or merged.")
    ap.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=40, help="Rows to include in markdown summary.")
    return ap.parse_args()


def safe_auc(y: pd.Series, x: pd.Series) -> float:
    mask = y.notna() & x.notna()
    if int(mask.sum()) < 8:
        return np.nan
    if int(y[mask].nunique()) < 2:
        return np.nan
    try:
        auc = float(roc_auc_score(y[mask].astype(int), x[mask].astype(float)))
        return max(auc, 1.0 - auc)
    except Exception:
        return np.nan


def cohens_d(pos: pd.Series, neg: pd.Series) -> float:
    p = pd.to_numeric(pos, errors="coerce").dropna()
    n = pd.to_numeric(neg, errors="coerce").dropna()
    if len(p) < 2 or len(n) < 2:
        return np.nan
    p_var = float(p.var(ddof=1))
    n_var = float(n.var(ddof=1))
    pooled = ((len(p) - 1) * p_var + (len(n) - 1) * n_var) / max(1, len(p) + len(n) - 2)
    if pooled <= 0:
        return np.nan
    return float((p.mean() - n.mean()) / np.sqrt(pooled))


def analyze_feature(df: pd.DataFrame, feature: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    s = pd.to_numeric(df[feature], errors="coerce")
    y = df["label"].astype(int)
    pos = s[y == 1]
    neg = s[y == 0]
    valid = s.notna()
    pos_missing = float((~valid & (y == 1)).sum() / max(1, (y == 1).sum()))
    neg_missing = float((~valid & (y == 0)).sum() / max(1, (y == 0).sum()))
    return {
        "feature": feature,
        "count_non_null": int(valid.sum()),
        "auc_abs": safe_auc(y, s),
        "cohens_d": cohens_d(pos, neg),
        "mean_pos": float(pos.mean()) if pos.notna().any() else np.nan,
        "mean_neg": float(neg.mean()) if neg.notna().any() else np.nan,
        "median_pos": float(pos.median()) if pos.notna().any() else np.nan,
        "median_neg": float(neg.median()) if neg.notna().any() else np.nan,
        "median_gap": float(pos.median() - neg.median()) if pos.notna().any() and neg.notna().any() else np.nan,
        "p90_pos": float(pos.quantile(0.9)) if pos.notna().any() else np.nan,
        "p90_neg": float(neg.quantile(0.9)) if neg.notna().any() else np.nan,
        "missing_rate_pos": pos_missing,
        "missing_rate_neg": neg_missing,
        "missing_gap": float(pos_missing - neg_missing),
    }


def main() -> int:
    args = parse_args()
    train_mode = resolve_train_data_mode(args.train_data)
    data_path = player_features_path(PROCESSED_ROOT, train_mode)
    if not data_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Training table not found for mode={train_mode}: {data_path}")

    df = pd.read_parquet(data_path)
    df = df[df["label"].notna()].copy()
    df["label"] = df["label"].astype(int)
    if "n_players" in df.columns:
        before = len(df)
        df = df[df["n_players"] >= 8].copy()
        print(f"[INFO] n_players>=8 filter: {before}->{len(df)} rows")

    exclude = {"label", "demo_id", "map_name", "attacker_name", "attacker_steamid", "dataset_source"}
    feature_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c not in exclude and pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[c])]
    ensure_no_forbidden_features(feature_cols, "feature separation analysis")

    rows = [analyze_feature(df, c) for c in feature_cols]
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    out["abs_cohens_d"] = out["cohens_d"].abs()
    out = out.sort_values(["auc_abs", "abs_cohens_d", "count_non_null"], ascending=[False, False, False]).reset_index(drop=True)

    REPORTS_ROOT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    csv_path = REPORTS_ROOT / f"feature_separation_{train_mode}.csv"
    md_path = REPORTS_ROOT / f"feature_separation_{train_mode}.md"
    json_path = REPORTS_ROOT / f"feature_separation_{train_mode}.json"
    out.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)

    top = out.head(int(args.top_k)).copy()
    lines = [
        "# Feature Separation",
        "",
        f"Mode: `{train_mode}`",
        "",
        f"Rows: {len(df)}  Demos: {df['demo_id'].nunique()}  Positives: {(df['label'] == 1).sum()}  Negatives: {(df['label'] == 0).sum()}",
        "",
        "| Feature | AUC* | |d| | Median+ | Median- | Missing+ | Missing- |",
        "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |",
    ]
    for _, row in top.iterrows():
        lines.append(
            "| {feature} | {auc_abs:.4f} | {abs_cohens_d:.4f} | {median_pos:.4f} | {median_neg:.4f} | {missing_rate_pos:.3f} | {missing_rate_neg:.3f} |".format(
                **row.to_dict()
            )
        )
    md_path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    summary = {
        "train_data_mode": train_mode,
        "data_path": str(data_path),
        "rows": int(len(df)),
        "demos": int(df["demo_id"].nunique()),
        "positives": int((df["label"] == 1).sum()),
        "negatives": int((df["label"] == 0).sum()),
        "top_features_by_auc_abs": top.head(20)["feature"].tolist(),
        "artifacts": {
            "csv": str(csv_path),
            "md": str(md_path),
        },
    }
    json_path.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"[OK] wrote {csv_path}")
    print(f"[OK] wrote {md_path}")
    print(f"[OK] wrote {json_path}")
    print("[TOP]")
    print(top[["feature", "auc_abs", "abs_cohens_d", "median_pos", "median_neg"]].head(15).to_string(index=False))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
